title: Bounded multiplication routine
statement: Fix a natural number $E$, an oracle assigning a Boolean value to each pair of an index in a four-element set and a finite Boolean word, an input Boolean word $x$, and a natural-number bound $B$. For either Boolean choice $f$ and any register state $st$ whose counter, scratch accumulator, and copy-and-shift scratch register are all zero, suppose every register value is at most $B$ and the product of the power accumulator with itself when $f$ is true, and with the base register when $f$ is false, is at most $B$. Then the machine reaches the exit state of the corresponding transfer move, with the power accumulator equal to that product; at each configuration strictly before the endpoint, the machine's validity conditions hold and every register remains at most $B$.
hypotheses_covered: The oracle has four indices and takes finite Boolean words
The copy-and-shift scratch register is zero
Every register value in $st$ is at most $B$
The specified product is at most $B
replaced:
Fix a Savitch register machine parameter $E$, an oracle, an input, and a register bound
$B$. For either choice of multiplier—using the base register or the power register—if
the counter, product accumulator, and scratch register start at $0$, every register
initially is at most $B$, and the resulting product is at most $B$, then the
multiplication routine reaches its exit label with the power register equal to that
product. At every configuration strictly before termination, the machine's validity
conditions hold and every register is at most $B$.
